plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with cup-shaped blooms on sturdy stems above strap-like blue-green leaves. Late-season tulips reach peak display in early May in cool temperate gardens and in famous bulb fields.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-spring to late spring (April to May in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Netherlands, northern Europe, northern United States, and Canada (cultivated); native to Central Asia
plants.funFact: During the 'Tulip Mania' of the 1630s in the Dutch Republic, single bulbs sold for more than the price of a luxury canal house.

plants.name: Wisteria sinensis
plants.description: A vigorous woody climbing vine that produces long, pendulous clusters of fragrant pea-like flowers before or as its leaves emerge. It can climb tall structures and live for decades.
plants.location: Native to China; widely cultivated in Japan, Europe, and the eastern and southern United States
plants.funFact: Chinese wisteria twines counterclockwise, while Japanese wisteria twines clockwise, which is a handy way to tell them apart.

plants.name: Hyacinthoides non-scripta
plants.description: A bulbous woodland perennial that carpets forest floors with nodding, bell-shaped flowers all arching to one side of the stem. Ancient woodlands are especially rich in bluebells.
plants.location: Western Europe, especially the United Kingdom and Ireland, in ancient deciduous woodlands
plants.funFact: The United Kingdom holds around half of the world's bluebell population, and it is illegal to dig up wild bluebells for sale there.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A tropical to subtropical tree with fern-like leaves that bursts into clouds of trumpet-shaped flowers. In the Southern Hemisphere, some regions have a second, lighter bloom, while in the tropics trees may flower in late spring and early summer. In places like parts of Florida and southern Asia, flowering begins around this time.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Northern Hemisphere; October to November in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to South America; cultivated in Florida, Hawaii, southern California, India, and parts of Africa
plants.funFact: Fallen jacaranda blossoms create purple carpets on streets, and in Pretoria, South Africa, it is known as the 'Jacaranda City' for its tens of thousands of trees.
